text:
Alex Chen: Observed a regression on hostpool-12 during the NF4 rollout. Short sequences + small batches hit ~10% throughput drop and occasional +1.6-2.0GB memory spikes. Posting quick flame and a few traces we grabbed.

Alex Chen: ```
flame: kernel_selector -> prefilter -> choose_kernel(nf4_qk_fast)
hot: conv_gemm(38%) | kv_copy(24%) | host_memcpy(16%)
context: seq<=64, batch<=8, hostpool-12
```

Jordan Liu: Can we get the selector debug for a few slow traces? Want to know if calibration shifted scores.

Mira Patel: Pasted selector evaluation for sample req (ts 2710032102):

Mira Patel: ```
features: {seq:32, batch:4, kv_hit:0.0, kv_frag:0.12, hw:a100-avax}
scores: {nf4_qk_fast:0.82, nf4_precise:0.66, fp4_small:0.70}
chosen: nf4_qk_fast
```

Samir K.: The kv_frag figure matters here. Prefill path + tiny batches can leave micro-fragments; certain nf4 fast kernels expect different slab alignment and we can end up with an extra host<->device memcpy per request. That would explain latency and the transient memory churn.

perf-bot: Canary summary (30m, short-seq focus):

perf-bot: ```
baseline: p95=76ms, tput=125 req/s
canary(nf4-calib): p95=88ms (+16%), tput=110 req/s (-12%), mem-mean=5.1GB (+1.6GB spikes)
```

Jordan Liu: If nf4_qk_fast triggers the memcpy, quick mitigation is to deprioritize it for small batches. Prefer a narrow selector rule rather than full rollback.

Alex Chen: Agreed. Proposal: add a temporary selector adjustment: score(nf4_qk_fast) -= 0.25 when batch<=8 && seq<=64 on hostpool-12. Run 30m, re-evaluate.

Mira Patel: I'll push the rule. Control-plane payload:

Mira Patel: ```bash
curl -X POST $CP/api/v1/selector-rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scope":"hostpool-12","condition":"batch<=8 && seq<=64","adjust":{"nf4_qk_fast":-0.25}}'
```

Samir K.: Also please collect lprof + kv-slab-stats for 2710032000-2710032400. Want to confirm whether fragment metrics and host memcpy counts drop after rule.

Alex Chen: @perf-bot can you run a targeted microbench (batch 1,4,8,16) with and without the rule and post delta?

perf-bot: Running microbench, ETA ~10m.

Mira Patel: I'll add a deterministic unit test in kernel-selector tomorrow that simulates prefill + small batches so future calibrations exercise this.

Samir K.: Local repro if anyone wants to run quickly:

Samir K.: ```bash
python -m bench.run --model nf4_candidate --batch 4 --seq 32 --prefill 1 --reps 300
```

perf-bot: Microbench results (median of 5 runs):

perf-bot: ```
without-rule: batch1 tput=420 rps, batch4 tput=130 rps, batch8 tput=92 rps
with-rule:    batch1 tput=430 rps (+2.4%), batch4 tput=145 rps (+11.5%), batch8 tput=105 rps (+14.1%)
notes: host memcpy count reduced ~35% for batch<=8, avg mem ~1.4GB lower
```

Jordan Liu: Nice. If telemetry shows memcpy drop and kv_frag improves, promote rule to wider canary and add selector unit test.

Alex Chen: Let's keep the rule live for 2 hours and then evaluate SLA metrics. If stable, backfill the change into the selector scoring model and add the test.

Mira Patel: Deployed the canary rule to hostpool-12 :rocket: lprof and slab stats link: https://lprof.internal/trace/2710032105 (private link)

Samir K.: Preliminary kv-slab snapshot before vs after:

Samir K.: ```
before: free_frag_ratio=0.07, avg_slab_rem=128 bytes, host_memcpy_count=18/min
after:  free_frag_ratio=0.11, avg_slab_rem=48 bytes,  host_memcpy_count=11/min
```

Alex Chen: Good signal. Also coordinate with runtime releases team so this selector change isn't lost on next rollout. Jordan can you add a short PR to the selector repo referencing this thread?

Jordan Liu: Will open PR with test fixture + note about prefill micro-exposure.

Mira Patel: Follow-up: consider a longer-term fix where kernel metadata includes expected slab alignment and the selector simulates slab outcome before choosing. That would avoid brittle heuristics. Filing RFC later this week.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Keep posting lprof links and if any regressions pop up roll back the rule immediately. :thumbsup:
